chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar from Ahmad ibn Muhammad said: He narrated to us from some of our companions, raising the hadith, saying:

Khums is due on five things: from the treasures, mines, diving (for pearls), the booty which is fought for, and the fifth was not preserved; and whatever was a conquest for which fighting did not occur and no cavalry or beasts of burden were marched upon it, except that our companions come to it and deal with it regarding it, so whatever they deal with it for, half or a third or a quarter or whatever is specifically allotted to it, and no one has anything in it except what he gives from it, and the bottoms of valleys, tops of mountains, and dead land, all of it is for him.
And this is His Exalted Saying, 'They ask you about the spoils of war,' meaning to give them from it, he said, 'Say: The spoils belong to Allah and the Messenger.'
And it is not 'They ask you about the spoils,' and whatever is of the cities and the inheritance of one who has no heir, it is for him specifically.
And this is His Mighty and Majestic Saying, 'What Allah has bestowed upon His Messenger from the people of the cities.'

As for Khums, it is divided into six shares: a share for Allah, a share for the Messenger (peace be upon him and his family), a share for the near relatives, a share for the orphans, a share for the poor, and a share for the wayfarer.

That which is for Allah and for the Messenger (peace be upon him and his family), the Messenger is more entitled to it, so it is for him specifically; and that which is for the Messenger is for the near relatives and the Proof in his time.
So half is for him specifically, and half is for the orphans, the poor, and the wayfarer from the Family of Muhammad (peace be upon them), who are not entitled to receive Zakat.

Allah compensated them in place of that with Khums, so He gives them according to their need. If something remains from it, it is for him; and if it falls short of their need and does not suffice them, he completes it for them from himself, just as the surplus becomes his, so the deficit is incumbent upon him.
ai.seo_question: What are the five items subject to Khums and how is it distributed among the Imams and the poor?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elaborates on the five categories of Khums, notably including unfortified conquests (*Fay'*) and barren lands, while clarifying the distribution into six shares. It establishes the theological basis for the Imams' exclusive right to Khums, distinguishing it from Zakat as a divine sustenance (*Kifayah*) for the Ahl al-Bayt, where any surplus reverts to the Imam and any deficit is covered by him.
